Scope: Static publisher-page and retained-artifact review of NTCore SNSRemover and WIM Installer for version, licensing, nested components, mutation and system-image effects; no payload executed or image/assembly modified

PublisherEvidence.Observation: The NTCore utility listing dates WIM Installer to 2007-04-21 and describes a GUI for setups based on WIM images, regardless of publisher. It dates SNSRemover to 2005-11-29 and says it removes strong-name signatures from .NET assemblies; the listed build is plain Win32 and does not require .NET Framework 2.0. No product-specific license/redistribution grant or current Windows target list is stated for either item.

PinnedArtifacts.NestedComponentObservation: The nested PE_Detective.zip hash differs from the separately reviewed standalone candidate; retain as a distinct older embedded artifact and do not silently substitute it.

ReviewFindings: Both archive length/SHA256 pins were recomputed and match the frozen inventory. No artifact was downloaded during this review; an attempted browser navigation to a publisher download endpoint returned a cache miss, so the retained local pin remained the only artifact inspected.

SNSRemover's published purpose changes a .NET assembly's strong-name signature. Input mutation versus distinct-output behavior, signature/key identity effects, delay-signing handling, managed-load behavior and recovery are unspecified. Use only an owned synthetic assembly and separate output in later review; preserve original bytes and verify signatures before/after.

SNSRemover.zip includes a PE_Detective.zip with a different hash and older contents than the standalone PE Detective selection. Do not replace or merge the separately pinned candidate based on the nested copy.

WIM Installer is a GUI for WIM-based setups, including images from non-Microsoft publishers. The page and frozen archive inventory do not establish image source validation, target/destination selection, partition/boot effects, network behavior, rollback or recovery. Treat it as image deployment with potential destructive disk effects; no WIM, disk or destination was opened.
No explicit product-specific license, redistribution grant, or current Windows target support was found in the publisher listing or retained member inventories.

MigrationDisposition.Resolved: Current publisher purposes, archive pins, x86 WIM version and nested PE Detective hash distinction are recorded.
MigrationDisposition.Partial: Product-specific rights, exact assembly mutation/output behavior, input signatures, WIM target/disk/boot effects, validation and recovery, current targets, UI and activation remain unresolved.
Deferred: Do not modify real or third-party assemblies; later SNSRemover behavior testing requires synthetic owned assemblies, separate output and byte/signature recovery checks.
Do not open, mount or apply production WIM images. Any later acceptance needs an inert synthetic image, disposable virtual disk, explicit destination, full checkpoint and verified rollback.
Clarify product-specific licensing and current Windows support before admission.
MigrationDisposition.EstimateReason: Two product effect and archive boundaries are clarified, but no whole legacy outcome was accepted, retired or excluded; rights, target, recovery and runtime remain open.
